source_text: நான் இன்று காலை 8 மணிக்கு பள்ளிக்குப் போகிறேன்.
expected_behavior: Produce a natural English translation preserving the time (8 o'clock) and the activity (going to school).
references: I am going to school at 8 o'clock today morning.
I am going to school at 8 a.m. today.
Today I am going to school at 8 o'clock.
provenance_note: Authored for TEB v1.0.0; not taken from any published corpus.
annotation_notes: Simple declarative sentence; suitable as a warm-up item.

expected_behavior: Translate naturally, keeping the reported-speech structure.
references: She said good morning.
She wished good morning.
She said 'good morning'.
annotation_notes: 'சொன்னாள்' is feminine past tense; avoid gender-neutral mistranslation is acceptable but 'she' is the intended reading.

expected_behavior: Translate with the degree modifier 'very' and the adjective 'interesting'.
references: This book is very interesting.
This book is extremely interesting.
This book is most interesting.

expected_behavior: Translate preserving the NEGATION: the group is not going to the market today.
references: We are not going to the market today.
We are not going to the market today.
Today we are not going to the market.

value: going to the market today and
critical_constraints.description: Must not assert the opposite meaning.

annotation_notes: Critical negation test: dropping 'வதில்லை' reverses the meaning.

source_text: அவன் என்னை ஒரு புதிய கார் வாங்க உதவினான்.
expected_behavior: Translate preserving the helping relationship: he helped me buy a new car.
references: He helped me buy a new car.
He helped me to buy a new car.
He assisted me in buying a new car.
context: Past event with a helper and an object.
annotation_notes: Ensure subject/object roles are not swapped (he helped me, not I helped him).

expected_behavior: Translate as a polite evening greeting using the respectful 'you'.
references: Good evening, how are you?
Good evening, how are you doing?
Good evening. How are you?
annotation_notes: நீங்கள் is honorific plural; 'you' is correct, avoid 'you all' unless context demands.

source_text: இவ்வாறு பல சிக்கல்கள் இருந்தபோதிலும், அவர் வேலையை நேரத்தில் முடித்தார்.
expected_behavior: Translate preserving the concessive relation (although/even though) and on-time completion.
references: Although there were many complications, he completed the work on time.
Even though there were many complications, he finished the work on time.
Despite many complications, he completed the work on time.
context: Complex sentence with a concessive clause.
annotation_notes: முடித்தார் is honorific; translation may use neutral 'he' but must not downgrade to casual register.

expected_behavior: Translate preserving the named entity 'Chennai' and the profession 'doctor'.
references: My brother works as a doctor in Chennai.
My elder brother works as a doctor in Chennai.
My brother is a doctor in Chennai.
context: Family and profession statement with a place name.

critical_constraints.description: City name must be preserved exactly.

annotation_notes: அண்ணன் = elder brother; 'brother' is acceptable, 'elder brother' more precise.

source_text: பள்ளி முடிந்த பிறகு நான் பூங்காவுக்குச் சென்றேன்.
expected_behavior: Translate preserving the temporal order: after school ended, I went to the park.
references: After school ended, I went to the park.
I went to the park after school was over.
After school got over, I went to the park.
annotation_notes: Avoid reversing the order (went to the park, then school ended).

source_text: இந்த காபி மிகவும் காடி கொண்டது; எனக்கு இன்னும் ஒரு கோப்பை வேணும்.
expected_behavior: Translate both clauses, preserving the strong-coffee description and the request for another cup.
references: This coffee is very strong; I want another cup.
This coffee is very strong; I would like one more cup.
This coffee is very strong, and I need another cup.

critical_constraints.description: Request for one more cup must appear.

annotation_notes: காடி = strong (of coffee/tea); do not translate as 'bitter' without evidence.
